def: A model that predicts the target as a weighted sum of the features plus an intercept.
The actual value minus the model's prediction for one example.
The average of the squared residuals, the standard loss for fitting a regression.
Choosing the weights that minimise the mean squared error of a linear model.
The linear equations (A transpose A) w = A transpose y whose solution is the least-squares weight vector.
Minimising a loss by repeatedly stepping the parameters against the gradient.
The step size multiplying the gradient in each gradient descent update.
Features that are nearly linear combinations of each other, making individual coefficients unstable while predictions stay steady.
A classifier that sets the log-odds of the positive class equal to a weighted sum of the features.
The factor by which the odds of the outcome are multiplied when a feature rises by one unit, equal to the exponential of its logistic weight.
The function 1 / (1 + e^-z) that maps any real number to a probability between 0 and 1.
The average negative log-probability a model gave to the true labels, also called binary cross-entropy.
Gradient descent that uses the gradient of a small random batch of rows at each step instead of the whole dataset.
